text:
Predicates:
BasketballPlayer(x) ::: x is a professional basketball player.
American(x) ::: x is an American national.
CanJumpShot(x) ::: x can do jump shots.
Leap(x) ::: x leaps straight into the air.
ActivateLegs(x) ::: x activates their leg muscles.
Premises:
∃x (BasketballPlayer(x) ∧ ¬American(x)) ::: Some professional basketball players are not American nationals.
∀x (BasketballPlayer(x) → CanJumpShot(x)) ::: All professional basketball players can do jump shots.
∀x (CanJumpShot(x) → Leap(x)) ::: If someone can do jump shots, they leap straight into the air.
∀x (Leap(x) → ActivateLegs(x)) ::: If someone leaps straight into the air, they activate their leg muscles.
¬ActivateLegs(yuri) ::: Yuri does not activate his leg muscles.
Conclusion:
(¬American(yuri) ∧ BasketballPlayer(yuri)) → BasketballPlayer(yuri) ::: If Yuri is not an American professional basketball player, then Yuri is a professional basketball player.
